title: Understanding Racial Inequities in School Discipline (SOP89)

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a bi-weekly podcast from the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会推出的一档双周播客。

sentences.en: I'm your host, Caitlin Luna.
sentences.zh: 我是主持人凯特琳·卢纳。

sentences.en: Discipline in K-12 schools is not doled out equally, as Black students, boys, and students with disabilities are suspended and expelled at much higher rates than other students.
sentences.zh: K-12学校的纪律处分并不平等，黑人学生、男生以及残障学生被停学和开除的比例远高于其他学生。

sentences.en: That's according to a report released last year by the
sentences.zh: 这是根据去年由

sentences.en: Government Accountability Office.
sentences.zh: 政府问责局发布的一份报告得出的结论。

sentences.en: These types of harsh discipline are even occurring in preschools across America.
sentences.zh: 这类严厉的纪律处分甚至在美国各地的学前班中也在发生。

sentences.en: Any kind of punishment that takes a kid out of the classroom is known as exclusionary discipline, and it can have dire consequences on a child's future, including
sentences.zh: 任何将孩子赶出教室的惩罚方式都被称为排斥性纪律，它可能对孩子的未来产生可怕的后果，包括

sentences.en: putting him or her at higher risk of falling into the school-to-prison pipeline.
sentences.zh: 使他们陷入“从学校到监狱”管道的风险更高。

sentences.en: Also looming around this issue is the fact that the Department of Education rolled back protections intended to reduce these well-documented disparities in December 2018.
sentences.zh: 此外，这一问题还笼罩在另一个事实之下：教育部在2018年12月撤销了旨在减少这些已有充分记录的差异的保护措施。

sentences.en: To explain the current state of school discipline and what we can do to help children have a fair shot at an education, our guests for
sentences.zh: 为了解释学校纪律的现状以及我们能做些什么来帮助孩子们获得公平的受教育机会，我们本期的嘉宾是

sentences.en: this episode are Dr. Amanda Sullivan, Associate Professor of Educational Psychology at the
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达大学教育心理学副教授阿曼达·沙利文博士，以及

sentences.en: University of Minnesota, and Dr. Ivory Toldson, Professor of Education at Howard University.
sentences.zh: 霍华德大学教育学教授艾弗里·托尔森博士。

sentences.en: Both are experts on discipline disparities in pre-K through 12 schools.
sentences.zh: 他们都是学前班到12年级学校纪律差异方面的专家。

sentences.en: They presented at a congressional briefing hosted by APA on the topic in June 2019.
sentences.zh: 2019年6月，他们在由美国心理学会主办的一次国会简报会上就该主题进行了发言。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Sullivan and Dr. Toldson.
sentences.zh: 欢迎二位，沙利文博士和托尔森博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: I'll start with you, Dr. Sullivan, firSt. You know, I gave a brief explanation of what the term
sentences.zh: 沙利文博士，先从您开始。您知道，我刚才简要解释了

sentences.en: exclusionary discipline means, but it will be helpful for you to expand on that a bit more for our listeners.
sentences.zh: “排斥性纪律”这个词的含义，但如果您能为我们的听众再详细展开讲讲，那将非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Yeah, certainly.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: So common practices include suspension and expulsion, which generally bar students return to school for a specified time period.
sentences.zh: 常见的做法包括停学和开除，这通常会禁止学生在特定时间内回到学校。

sentences.en: And this can be anywhere from days to the remainder of a school year.
sentences.zh: 时间跨度从几天到整个学年不等。

sentences.en: But it also includes things like early dismissal, so sending a child home with their parent off the record, or extended timeouts in school suspension, so spending the day or
sentences.zh: 但它也包括一些其他形式，比如提前放学，即在非正式记录的情况下让家长把孩子接回家，或者在校内进行长时间的禁闭，也就是在教室里待上一天或

sentences.en: several days in a room, kind of like what we almost think of as like study hall used to be.
sentences.zh: 几天，有点像我们过去认为的自习课。

sentences.en: But it can also include things like using physical restraint, corporal punishment, and even involving law enforcement.
sentences.zh: 它还可以包括使用身体约束、体罚，甚至动用执法部门。

sentences.en: And like you mentioned, taken together, it just shows this common feature of removing students from opportunities to learn.
sentences.zh: 正如您提到的，综合来看，这反映了一个共同特征，即剥夺了学生学习的机会。

sentences.en: And it's important to be aware that it happens at all age and grade levels.
sentences.zh: 而且必须意识到，这种情况发生在所有年龄段和年级。

sentences.en: So we see it used throughout elementary, middle, and secondary school, but also early childhood settings.
sentences.zh: 我们在小学、初中、高中，甚至幼儿教育环境中都能看到这种做法。

sentences.en: So these practices get applied with preschoolers, toddlers, and even infants to a certain extent.
sentences.zh: 这些做法在一定程度上被应用于学龄前儿童、幼儿，甚至婴儿身上。

sentences.en: Can you describe situations when this exclusionary discipline is used in schools?
sentences.zh: 您能描述一下学校在什么情况下会使用这种排斥性纪律吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: I mean, I think people have a misconception that it's reserved for very severe or dangerous
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为人们有一种误解，认为这只针对非常严重或危险的

sentences.en: behaviors, but we see it used for everything from tardiness to dress code violations, very kind of ambiguous or subjective offenses like disrespect or talking out of turn.
sentences.zh: 行为，但我们看到它被用于各种情况，从迟到到违反着装规范，甚至是一些非常模糊或主观的违规行为，比如不尊重老师或插话。

sentences.en: And so it really gets applied across the boards as oftentimes a kind of go-to response to any behavior that's unwanted in the school setting.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实被广泛应用，通常作为对学校中任何不受欢迎行为的“首选”应对方式。

sentences.en: And these disparities show that this practice is overused in our schools in America today.
sentences.zh: 这些差异表明，这种做法在当今美国的学校中被过度使用了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in many school systems, yes.
sentences.zh: 在许多学校系统中确实如此。

sentences.en: And is it ever an effective way to manage disruptive students?
sentences.zh: 那么，这对于管理捣乱的学生来说是一种有效的方法吗？

sentences.en: I mean, or some people who might argue for it in certain cases?
sentences.zh: 或者说，在某些情况下，是否有人会支持这种做法？

sentences.en: I think very rarely.
sentences.zh: 我认为极少有效。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the science of psychology has given us a lot of knowledge about how we respond effectively to both prevent inappropriate behaviors, but to foster positive
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，心理学科学已经为我们提供了大量知识，告诉我们如何有效地预防不当行为，并培养积极的

sentences.en: behaviors.
sentences.zh: 行为。

sentences.en: And in general, those are better options than any of these exclusionary discipline practices.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这些方法比任何排斥性纪律措施都要好。

sentences.en: I want to turn to that Government Accountability Office report, which found that black students comprised 15% of all public school students.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈那份政府问责局的报告，报告发现黑人学生占所有公立学校学生的15%。

sentences.en: Yet they accounted for 39% of all students suspended from school during the 2013-2014 school year.
sentences.zh: 然而，在2013-2014学年，他们占了所有被停学学生总数的39%。

sentences.en: That was the most recent data GAO had access to while doing its report.
sentences.zh: 这是政府问责局在撰写报告时能获取到的最新数据。

sentences.en: Do you believe that some of these, what are some of the underlying factors that are causing this, Dr. Tolson?
sentences.zh: 托尔森博士，您认为导致这种情况的根本因素有哪些？

sentences.en: Well, I think the main factor is that not enough people care.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为主要因素是关心的人不够多。

sentences.en: These statistics have been out for so long now, decades even.
sentences.zh: 这些统计数据已经公布很久了，甚至有几十年了。

sentences.en: It's consistent across so many different data sets, so many different reports are finding the exact same thing.
sentences.zh: 在许多不同的数据集和报告中，结论都是一致的，它们发现的都是完全相同的情况。

sentences.en: And there's just not enough people that care about the problem are who really believe that there are unfair reasons for this happening.
sentences.zh: 只是没有足够多的人关心这个问题，或者真正相信导致这种情况的原因是不公平的。

sentences.en: There's too many people out there that think that black boys just do more bad things, and that's why they're being suspended more.
sentences.zh: 有太多人认为黑人男孩就是更容易做坏事，所以他们才会被停学更多。

sentences.en: But beyond that, some of the factors that's shown up in research, there's a cultural mismatch between a lot of black students and the teachers that serve them.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，研究中显示的一些因素是，许多黑人学生与服务他们的老师之间存在文化错位。

sentences.en: And this isn't just based on race, it's also based on socioeconomic status.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅基于种族，也基于社会经济地位。

sentences.en: A lot of children who come from poor communities, they're taught by people who don't understand them very well and who have certain
sentences.zh: 许多来自贫困社区的孩子，教他们的老师并不太了解他们，并且对他们的社区、成长方式和家庭持有

sentences.en: stereotypes about their communities, how they grow up, their families.
sentences.zh: 某种刻板印象。

sentences.en: And these stereotypes manifest themselves in overly punitive disciplinary practices.
sentences.zh: 这些刻板印象体现在过度惩罚性的纪律措施中。

sentences.en: It also leads to a lot of educators believing that the children that they're teaching are threatening.
sentences.zh: 这也导致许多教育工作者认为他们所教的孩子具有威胁性。

sentences.en: And so, whereas a white girl in a suburban school, her attitude may be described as sassy.
sentences.zh: 所以，郊区学校里的一个白人女孩，她的态度可能会被描述为“活泼”。

sentences.en: A black boy in under-resourced school, that same disposition would be considered thuggish or those types of things.
sentences.zh: 而在资源匮乏学校里的一个黑人男孩，同样的性格会被认为是“暴徒”或类似的东西。

sentences.en: And that makes a difference in how people will view a problem.
sentences.zh: 这会影响人们看待问题的方式。

sentences.en: Another issue is one of the main factors that's associated with suspensions is academic disengagement.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，与停学相关的主要因素之一是学术参与度低下。

sentences.en: So, students who seem to care less about their particular school are more likely to be suspended.
sentences.zh: 所以，那些似乎不太关心学校的学生更容易被停学。

sentences.en: And you're more likely to care less if you're going to a school where you're passing through metal detectors, where you have this strict dress code policy,
sentences.zh: 如果你去的是一所需要通过金属探测器、有着严格着装规范的学校，

sentences.en: where you're not invited to express yourself as you go through this very important stage in your life.
sentences.zh: 而且在你人生中这个非常重要的阶段不被鼓励表达自我，那你自然更不会关心学校。

sentences.en: You're also not given a lot of agency into your own affairs, and you're not taught a curriculum that's culturally aligned to you.
sentences.zh: 你对自己事务的掌控权也很少，而且你所学的课程与你的文化背景并不契合。

sentences.en: And so, a lot of times these students will not engage as well, which leads to more punitive disciplinary policies.
sentences.zh: 因此，很多时候这些学生参与度不高，这又导致了更具惩罚性的纪律政策。

sentences.en: So, those are some of the underlying issues.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些就是一些根本问题。

sentences.en: Last point, black students are more likely to be suspended in predominantly black schools.
sentences.zh: 最后一点，黑人学生在以黑人为主的学校中更容易被停学。

sentences.en: When they go to integrated schools, they still get suspended proportionally more than the white students at those schools, but they get suspended less often
sentences.zh: 当他们进入综合性学校时，他们被停学的比例仍然高于那里的白人学生，但频率要比

sentences.en: than the black students at predominantly black schools.
sentences.zh: 在以黑人为主的学校中的黑人学生要低。

sentences.en: So, this demonstrates that a lot of times it has something to do with the culture of the school.
sentences.zh: 这表明，很多时候这与学校的文化有关。

sentences.en: When you have a predominantly black student body,
sentences.zh: 当学生群体以黑人为主时，

sentences.en: there's a certain attitude and mentality.
sentences.zh: 会有一种特定的态度和心态。

sentences.en: There's something that the educators are seeing that they should not see that's leading to these harsh policies.
sentences.zh: 教育工作者看到了一些他们不该看到的东西，从而导致了这些严厉的政策。

sentences.en: You touched on a very important point about implicit bias, and just a brief description,
sentences.zh: 您提到了一个非常重要的点，即隐性偏见，简单描述一下，

sentences.en: is that's when we have attitudes toward people or associate stereotypes of them without being consciously aware of it.
sentences.zh: 就是我们在没有意识到的情况下，对人持有某种态度或联想到刻板印象。

sentences.en: So, can you elaborate more about how implicit bias factors into some of these disparities?
sentences.zh: 那么，您能详细说明一下隐性偏见是如何导致这些差异的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And implicit biases are biases that's beyond your conscious awareness.
sentences.zh: 隐性偏见是超出你意识范围的偏见。

sentences.en: They typically manifest themselves in decisions that you make without really thinking about them.
sentences.zh: 它们通常体现在你未经深思熟虑就做出的决定中。

sentences.en: And it's important for me to point out that while implicit biases are rampant, and I think that all of us
sentences.zh: 我必须指出，虽然隐性偏见非常普遍，而且我认为我们所有人

sentences.en: have implicit biases, I think that the explicit biases, the things that a lot of these educators will actually admit to, are actually just as severe or maybe even more.
sentences.zh: 都有隐性偏见，但我认为显性偏见——即许多教育工作者实际上会承认的那些东西——其实同样严重，甚至可能更严重。

sentences.en: So, when we hear educators talk about kids from that community, when they say all of them come from single-parent households, and that's why they act the way that they act.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们听到教育工作者谈论来自那个社区的孩子时，当他们说“他们都来自单亲家庭，所以才表现成那样”时。

sentences.en: When they say that, you know, none of these children are reading on grade levels, so why would we have science at this school?
sentences.zh: 当他们说，“你知道，这些孩子没有一个能达到年级阅读水平，所以我们学校为什么要开设科学课？”

sentences.en: Or why do we have, why would we even have calculus at this school?
sentences.zh: 或者“我们学校为什么要开设微积分？”

sentences.en: These are things I hear all the time.
sentences.zh: 这些话我经常听到。

sentences.en: And I think until we deal, you know, I wish we had the luxury to just zero in on implicit biases.
sentences.zh: 我认为在我们处理这些问题之前，你知道，我希望我们有余力只关注隐性偏见。

sentences.en: But a lot of this stuff is blatant, dare I say it, racism and racial explicit biases.
sentences.zh: 但很多这类事情是赤裸裸的，我敢说是种族主义和种族显性偏见。

sentences.en: And these explicit biases are, you said they're playing out in schools all across America today.
sentences.zh: 而这些显性偏见，正如您所说，正在当今美国各地的学校中上演。

sentences.en: Do you know, can you elaborate more about why black boys would be more likely to be expelled from all black school or predominantly African American schools?
sentences.zh: 您知道，您能详细说明一下为什么黑人男孩在全黑人学校或以非裔美国人为主的学校中更容易被开除吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it has to do with the way that people see the school environment.
sentences.zh: 是的，这与人们看待学校环境的方式有关。

sentences.en: A lot of times when we think about suspensions, we think about it as on an individual level.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，当我们想到停学时，我们是从个人层面去考虑的。

sentences.en: We don't think of it as on a systemic level.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有从系统层面去思考。

sentences.en: And this makes us think that there's certain children that are more likely to be suspended, certain teachers who are more likely to give referrals or send children out of class.
sentences.zh: 这让我们认为有些孩子更容易被停学，有些老师更容易给出处分或把孩子赶出教室。

sentences.en: But really, it's a larger structure.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这是一个更大的结构性问题。

sentences.en: And that's something that we have to understand.
sentences.zh: 这是我们必须理解的。

sentences.en: Typically, when you have a diverse school environment or have, especially an environment that has a lot of affluent children, children with parents with means, the school
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，当你拥有一个多元化的学校环境，或者特别是拥有许多富裕家庭孩子、父母有经济实力的环境时，学校

sentences.en: will accommodate those students in ways that they won't accommodate poor students.
sentences.zh: 会以他们不会对待贫困学生的方式来迁就这些学生。

sentences.en: And they also perceive their behaviors or they perceive the overall school environment as an environment that is conducive to learning.
sentences.zh: 他们也会认为这些学生的行为或整体学校环境是有利于学习的。

sentences.en: A lot of times, we have principals that are assigned to predominantly black school because the people that hired them believe that there are discipline probleMs. You rarely see
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我们指派到以黑人为主的学校的校长，是因为雇佣他们的人认为那里有纪律问题。你很少看到

sentences.en: a principal coming to a predominantly white school just to just because they are a good disciplinarian.
sentences.zh: 一位校长仅仅因为擅长管纪律就被派往以白人为主的学校。

sentences.en: They go there because they know how to make that connection between what they're learning in school and going to college and different things like that.
sentences.zh: 他们去那里是因为他们知道如何将学校所学与升学等事情联系起来。

sentences.en: So what we need to assert and demand is that predominantly black schools need the same type of resources, the same mentality, the same care that
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要主张并要求，以黑人为主的学校需要与

sentences.en: the predominantly white schools are having.
sentences.zh: 以白人为主的学校获得同样的资源、同样的理念和同样的关怀。

sentences.en: And to assign a coach to be principal of a predominantly black school because they tough talk and because they talk about putting students in line, that demonstrates a
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为某位教练说话强硬、谈论如何让学生“排好队”就指派他担任以黑人为主的学校的校长，这本身就体现了一种

sentences.en: bias in and of itself.
sentences.zh: 偏见。

sentences.en: And it usually leads to the strict disciplinary policies that we see.
sentences.zh: 而且这通常会导致我们所看到的那些严格的纪律政策。

sentences.en: Yeah, we also see that behaviors are treated very differently and perceived very differently.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们也看到行为被对待和感知的方式截然不同。

sentences.en: I mean, from an early childhood onward.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从幼儿时期开始就是这样。

sentences.en: So we can look at like research that's used eye tracking shows that educators tend to spend more time watching the black students in a classroom.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看看那些使用眼动追踪的研究，它显示教育工作者往往花更多时间盯着教室里的黑人学生。

sentences.en: So they're looking for trouble.
sentences.zh: 他们在寻找麻烦。

sentences.en: And then when something does occur, it's perceived differently, like Dr. Tolson mentioned.
sentences.zh: 当事情真的发生时，正如托尔森博士所提到的，感知方式也不同。

sentences.en: And so there's more, there's more observation of these students.
sentences.zh: 所以对这些学生的观察更多。

sentences.en: But then regardless of what they do, again, anything from disobedience or speaking out of turn, that kind of thing, the harsher discipline tends to get applied.
sentences.zh: 但无论他们做什么，再次强调，从不服从到插话，诸如此类，往往会受到更严厉的纪律处分。

sentences.en: So when we look at the research that has looked at like what happens to students when decisions are made, white students tend to be penalized for much more
sentences.zh: 所以当我们审视那些研究学生在决策过程中遭遇的研究时，白人学生往往因为更

sentences.en: severe behaviors, whereas students of color are more likely to be penalized for things that are very much judgment calls around what's acceptable.
sentences.zh: 严重的行为受到惩罚，而有色人种学生更容易因为那些完全取决于对“什么是可接受的”判断的行为而受到惩罚。

sentences.en: And oftentimes things that are actually acceptable and adaptive in their communities are the things they're getting punished for in schools.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，那些在他们社区中实际上是可以接受且具有适应性的行为，却成了他们在学校里受罚的原因。

sentences.en: And so I think a lot of things come back to misunderstandings of culture, misunderstandings of child development, behavior, learning and mental
sentences.zh: 所以我认为很多事情归根结底是对文化、儿童发展、行为、学习和心理健康的误解，

sentences.en: health, that then we're penalized, penalizing kids for the misunderstandings of the adults in the settings.
sentences.zh: 然后我们因为这些环境中的成年人的误解而惩罚孩子。

sentences.en: So this is a broader cultural issue in terms of we're saying it's, it's the culture of the school, it's the culture of the, you know, the people who are at the school.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个更广泛的文化问题，也就是说，这是学校的文化，是学校里的人的文化。

sentences.en: Or do you have examples off the top of your head of schools that are doing this, doing this well in terms of working to reduce these disparities?
sentences.zh: 或者您能随口举出一些在减少这些差异方面做得很好的学校例子吗？

sentences.en: Anything come to mind?
sentences.zh: 有什么想到的吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think schools where they're, they're actually attending to it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为那些真正关注这个问题的学校做得不错。

sentences.en: So monitoring their data, not just by race, but gender, disability status,
sentences.zh: 比如不仅按种族，还按性别、残障状况来监测他们的数据，

sentences.en: where they are investing in staff training to develop non-biased attitudes to engage in non-discriminatory practices.
sentences.zh: 并且投资于员工培训，以培养无偏见的态度，参与非歧视性的实践。

sentences.en: We see some really nice successes with investments in positive school climate, in developing student engagement, in using school-wide positive behavioral interventions
sentences.zh: 我们看到在投资于积极的学校氛围、发展学生参与度、使用全校范围的积极行为干预

sentences.en: and supports, where the focus there is on teaching and reinforcing positive behaviors as opposed to just
sentences.zh: 和支持方面取得了一些非常好的成功，其重点在于教授和强化积极行为，而不是仅仅

sentences.en: punishing and, in particular, sending kids out because of unwanted behaviors.
sentences.zh: 惩罚，特别是仅仅因为不受欢迎的行为就把孩子赶走。

sentences.en: So it all starts with teaching.
sentences.zh: 所以一切都从教学开始。

sentences.en: We don't expect students to magically come to school knowing how to read.
sentences.zh: 我们不会指望学生神奇地来到学校就学会了阅读。

sentences.en: So why would we think that they would walk into a classroom magically knowing how a teacher wants them to behave?
sentences.zh: 那么我们为什么会认为他们走进教室就能神奇地知道老师希望他们如何表现呢？

sentences.en: And I'll add that it's probably more common than a lot of people think to have a school that have disciplinary policies that are fair.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点，拥有公平纪律政策的学校可能比许多人想象的要普遍。

sentences.en: And a lot of times it starts with the principal.
sentences.zh: 很多时候这始于校长。

sentences.en: Teachers do not have the authority to suspend students.
sentences.zh: 老师没有权力停学学生。

sentences.en: It's the assistant principal typically that, that makes that decision.
sentences.zh: 通常是副校长做出那个决定。

sentences.en: But the teachers are the ones sending the students out.
sentences.zh: 但老师是把学生送出去的人。

sentences.en: But it's really the principal that sets the tone.
sentences.zh: 但真正定下基调的是校长。

sentences.en: If the principal comes in day one and says, we're going to keep these students in our class.
sentences.zh: 如果校长第一天就说，我们要把这些学生留在课堂里。

sentences.en: And these are, these are the resources I'm giving you.
sentences.zh: 这些是我提供给你们的资源。

sentences.en: This is what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们要做的。

sentences.en: It typically happens.
sentences.zh: 通常情况就会好转。

sentences.en: And, you know, there are programs out there, restorative justice.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，市面上有一些项目，比如恢复性司法。

sentences.en: And I think those programs work very well.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些项目效果很好。

sentences.en: But I think it's also a mistake that a lot of people make thinking that predominantly black schools need something differently than predominantly white schools.
sentences.zh: 但我认为很多人犯了一个错误，认为以黑人为主的学校需要与以白人为主的学校不同的东西。

sentences.en: If you look at the way that they typically handle some of the same types of issues at
sentences.zh: 如果你看看他们通常处理同样类型问题的方式，在

sentences.en: predominantly white schools, if we just look at dress code policies, a lot of suburban, predominantly
sentences.zh: 以白人为主的学校，如果我们只看着装规范政策，许多郊区的、以白人为主的

sentences.en: white schools, their dress code policies are very loose, and they would never send a child home over dress codes.
sentences.zh: 学校，他们的着装规范非常宽松，他们绝不会因为着装规范而让孩子回家。

sentences.en: But in a lot of the impoverished, predominantly black areas, it's common.
sentences.zh: 但在许多贫困的、以黑人为主的地区，这很常见。

sentences.en: So just that alone will reduce suspensions.
sentences.zh: 所以仅此一点就能减少停学。

sentences.en: And we could just go down the list, look at how you, you know, so, so my, my method, what I would tell people to do, what would you do if the student was white?
sentences.zh: 我们可以列举下去，看看你怎么做，你知道，所以，我的方法，我会告诉人们去做的是：如果这个学生是白人，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: Honestly.
sentences.zh: 说实话。

sentences.en: And I think we could fix a lot of things just that way.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们完全可以通过这种方式解决很多问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I remember there was a, an issue a couple months ago of a school in Houston, I believe, where there was a dress code for parents.
sentences.zh: 我记得几个月前，休斯顿有所学校出过一个问题，我想应该是关于家长着装规范的。

sentences.en: And that created a lot of controversy because parents were, you know, dropping their children off.
sentences.zh: 那件事引起了很大的争议，因为家长们当时正在送孩子上学。

sentences.en: Maybe they'd just gotten up in the morning or something.
sentences.zh: 也许他们只是刚起床之类的。

sentences.en: And the issue was that the principal did not want parents to come to school in, I guess, you may call pajamas or relaxed clothing, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 问题在于校长不想让家长穿着，我想你可以称之为睡衣或休闲服之类的衣服来学校。

sentences.en: So what kind of message would something even like that send?
sentences.zh: 那么，像这样的事情会传递出什么样的信息呢？

sentences.en: And I'll be remiss if I, if I didn't say that, that was a black principal.
sentences.zh: 如果我不提的话，我会有失职之嫌，那就是那位校长是一位黑人。

sentences.en: It was a predominantly, predominantly students of color, black and Hispanic.
sentences.zh: 那所学校的学生主要是少数族裔，黑人和西班牙裔。

sentences.en: And they have a fair number of black teachers, and a good number of black people who supported that decision.
sentences.zh: 他们有相当多的黑人教师，也有不少黑人支持那个决定。

sentences.en: And it goes to show that, uh, even black people, uh, can be biased against other black people, particularly poor people.
sentences.zh: 这表明，即使是黑人，也可能对其他黑人，特别是贫困的黑人抱有偏见。

sentences.en: Um, and I, I think that this idea that certain children come from certain neighborhoods
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这种观念，即某些孩子来自某些社区，

sentences.en: that have these corrupted cultural values and somehow they need to be put in line in order for them, uh, to achieve.
sentences.zh: 拥有这些腐化的价值观，为了让他们取得成就，必须以某种方式让他们守规矩。

sentences.en: Uh, so, you know, if you're in a predominantly white neighborhood, uh, you know, a gentrifying
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你在一个以白人为主的社区，一个正在中产阶级化的社区，

sentences.en: neighborhood and your parents are coming with flip-flops and, uh, they didn't dry their hair.
sentences.zh: 而你的父母穿着人字拖来了，而且他们没吹干头发。

sentences.en: So it's wet hair.
sentences.zh: 头发是湿的。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 那没关系。

sentences.en: But if you have a black woman that comes in rollers, somehow they, they're extending
sentences.zh: 但如果是一个戴着卷发筒的黑人女性进来，他们不知怎么地就把这种观念延伸了，

sentences.en: this way beyond, um, just a, uh, a woman bringing her child to school, uh, and wanting her curls to be fresher when she gets to work than when she drops the kids off.
sentences.zh: 远远超出了一个母亲送孩子上学，想让自己的卷发在上班时比送孩子时看起来更清爽的范畴。

sentences.en: Um, so there, there's, there's this larger mentality that we have, uh, and it's not just race, it's class, uh, that we really need to, to, to check.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，我们有一种更宏大的心态，这不仅仅是种族问题，更是阶级问题，我们真的需要审视一下。

sentences.en: I think it's just an extension of this notion of like respectability politics in schools.
sentences.zh: 我认为这只是学校里那种“体面政治”观念的延伸。

sentences.en: And so it's not just schools trying to control and shape the behaviors of kids, but then we see it extending to the parents as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，这不仅仅是学校试图控制和塑造孩子的行为，我们还看到这种控制延伸到了家长身上。

sentences.en: I want to turn over to boys, um, because in the report, they were particularly overrepresented among students who received corporal punishment,
sentences.zh: 我想转到男孩的话题上，因为在报告中，他们在接受体罚的学生中比例特别高，

sentences.en: physical punishment by about 27 percentage points.
sentences.zh: 体罚率高出约27个百分点。

sentences.en: And when I read the statistic, I was quite surprised because I thought corporal punishment was a thing of the paSt. So how are
sentences.zh: 当我读到这个统计数据时，我非常惊讶，因为我以为体罚已经是过去式了。那么，

sentences.en: schools able to administer physical punishment and in what types of schools is this happening in and where are they around the country?
sentences.zh: 学校是如何实施体罚的？这种事发生在什么样的学校？在全国范围内分布在哪里？

sentences.en: I mean, it's still legal in, I want to say about 19 or 20 states.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它在我想大概19或20个州仍然是合法的。

sentences.en: So it's, they're not violating any laws if they, they use corporal punishment.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他们使用体罚，并没有违反任何法律。

sentences.en: Um, it's, it's allowed, I, I am fairly certain it's more common in the South, um, which is true for a lot of the more severe exclusionary discipline practices.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是允许的。我相当肯定它在南部更常见，这对于许多更严重的排斥性纪律处分来说也是如此。

sentences.en: We tend to see higher levels, um, in that part of the country.
sentences.zh: 我们往往在该地区看到更高水平的此类处分。

sentences.en: Um, but in a lot of ways, it's an extension of the same way we see differences regionally and,
sentences.zh: 嗯，但在很多方面，这是我们所看到的区域性差异的延伸，

sentences.en: and, and certain groups around acceptance of corporal punishment at home, um, that permissiveness extends into the schools again.
sentences.zh: 以及某些群体对家庭体罚的接受程度，这种宽容再次延伸到了学校。

sentences.en: And so it's not uncommon to see not just acceptance, but preference for that kind of response to misbehaviors in school settings.
sentences.zh: 因此，在学校环境中，不仅接受，甚至偏好这种应对不当行为的方式并不罕见。

sentences.en: But again, it's, it's legal in many states today right now.
sentences.zh: 但再说一次，它在今天许多州仍然是合法的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I found that to be quite shocking, um, that that was even a thing people were doing in schools.
sentences.zh: 我发现这相当令人震惊，人们竟然还在学校里这样做。

sentences.en: Do you have anything to add Dr. Tolson?
sentences.zh: Tolson博士，你有什么要补充的吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And, and it's, it's not common.
sentences.zh: 而且，这并不常见。

sentences.en: It's, it's far more common to bring police officers in the school and arrest students for very innocuous behaviors.
sentences.zh: 更常见的是把警察带进学校，因为非常轻微的行为就逮捕学生。

sentences.en: Uh, and that's, um, much more of an imminent threat, uh, to us, but there are these pockets out there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对我们来说是一个更迫在眉睫的威胁，但确实存在这些零星的现象。

sentences.en: Um, there, uh, you know, as Dr. Sullivan said, there's probably about 19 states and they're all listed online.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如Sullivan博士所说，大概有19个州，网上都有列出。

sentences.en: They're pretty easy to, to find with a Google search.
sentences.zh: 通过谷歌搜索很容易找到。

sentences.en: Um, a lot of the states where it's legal, they still don't implement it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在许多体罚合法的州，他们实际上并不实施。

sentences.en: And a lot of times you still have to have parents permission to do it.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候你仍然需要家长的许可才能这样做。

sentences.en: Um, but as with all of the different types of exclusionary, uh, are highly overly punitive policies.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但就像所有不同类型的排斥性或过度惩罚政策一样，

sentences.en: We see disproportionality when it comes to, uh, black students, uh, in particular black male students.
sentences.zh: 我们在黑人学生，特别是黑人男学生身上看到了这种不成比例的现象。

sentences.en: Can you touch on the arrest in school you just mentioned?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈你刚才提到的学校逮捕事件吗？

sentences.en: Like, what are we seeing, you know, bringing police officers to the school to remove students?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们所看到的，把警察带到学校带走学生是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Or if there's an in the school security officer that's involved with removing a student from the classroom, what kind of rates are we seeing this happening in?
sentences.zh: 或者如果有校内保安参与将学生从教室带走，我们看到的发生率是多少？

sentences.en: Um, very high.
sentences.zh: 嗯，非常高。

sentences.en: Uh, and you know, these are some of the things that a lot of people probably don't, don't, weren't aware of.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，这些是很多人可能并不了解的事情。

sentences.en: Um, but most school resource officers are academy trained police officers with arresting authority and they have no further
sentences.zh: 嗯，但大多数学校资源官员都是受过学院培训的警察，拥有逮捕权，他们并没有比任何追捕商店扒手或抢劫犯的人，

sentences.en: training to, to, to work in schools, uh, than anybody out there chasing, um, people who shoplift or who mug somebody.
sentences.zh: 接受过更多在学校工作的培训。

sentences.en: Um, a lot of times the school resource officers are assigned there because there's no other good fit for them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，很多时候学校资源官员被分配到那里是因为没有其他适合他们的岗位。

sentences.en: So they're not people who just say, I love children and I want to work around kids.
sentences.zh: 所以他们并不是那种说“我热爱孩子，我想在孩子身边工作”的人。

sentences.en: Uh, these are people who, for whatever reason, usually pretty nebulous reasons are assigned to the school.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些人通常因为各种原因，通常是非常模糊的原因，被分配到学校。

sentences.en: Um, another thing is that a lot of them are, are armed, uh, correctional officers in the prison don't carry guns and they're not academy trained.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还有一件事是他们很多人都携带武器，监狱里的惩教人员不携带枪支，他们也没有受过学院培训。

sentences.en: They're trained specifically to work with that population.
sentences.zh: 他们受过专门的培训来处理那类人群。

sentences.en: Um, the police officers in school are armed and they can make arreSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，学校里的警察携带武器，他们可以进行逮捕。

sentences.en: And then you have these laws, you have, you have these, the, these school conduct laws, like what
sentences.zh: 然后你就有这些法律，你有这些学校行为准则法律，就像南卡罗来纳州发生的那样，

sentences.en: happened in, in, in South Carolina, where the, the officer body slammed the, the, the young girl, uh, and it was caught on camera.
sentences.zh: 那个警察把那个年轻女孩摔在地上，而且被摄像机拍到了。

sentences.en: Um, but in South Carolina, there is a law that makes discipline problematic behavior in school.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但在南卡罗来纳州，有一项法律规定学校里的纪律问题行为是违法的。

sentences.en: Um, and they actually use the word obnoxiously in the law.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们在法律中甚至使用了“令人厌恶地”这个词。

sentences.en: So someone who's acting obnoxiously in the school is subject to arreSt. So that makes things that you can do outside of
sentences.zh: 所以，在学校里表现得令人厌恶的人可能会被逮捕。这使得你在校外可以做的事情，

sentences.en: school, you know, so the same black girl could go to a store and catch an attitude with a clerk and that would not be an arrestable offense, but you do it in school.
sentences.zh: 你知道，同一个黑人女孩去商店对店员摆脸色，那不会是可逮捕的罪行，但你在学校里这样做，

sentences.en: And all of a sudden you have a officer body slamming you, um, are just arresting you.
sentences.zh: 突然之间你就有了一个警察把你摔在地上，或者只是逮捕你。

sentences.en: Uh, so we've really gotten far away from where we need to go.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我们真的偏离了我们应该前进的方向。

sentences.en: And, and, and, and the, the irony is a lot of these laws originate from a lot of mass
sentences.zh: 而且，讽刺的是，许多这些法律源于许多校园大规模枪击事件，

sentences.en: shootings at school, which are more often at predominantly white schools, but yet the laws end up morphing and
sentences.zh: 这些事件更多发生在以白人为主的学校，但法律最终却发生了演变，

sentences.en: end up disproportionately affecting black students, even though the behaviors of black students wasn't necessarily the original impetus to the law.
sentences.zh: 最终不成比例地影响了黑人学生，尽管黑人学生的行为并不一定是该法律的初衷。

sentences.en: So it's a, it's a lot of things we need to think about when it comes to the way that we're using school resource officers right now.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们谈到目前使用学校资源官员的方式时，有很多事情我们需要思考。

sentences.en: My personal opinion is that we need to do away with school resource officers altogether.
sentences.zh: 我个人的观点是，我们需要彻底取消学校资源官员。

sentences.en: Uh, that may be a radical thing for some people to hear, but if you're going to have a school security officer, they need to be trained to work in a school.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对某些人来说可能是一个激进的观点，但如果你要设立学校保安，他们需要接受在学校工作的培训。

sentences.en: And across the nation, you have people who have, who have no training to work in schools.
sentences.zh: 而在全国范围内，你拥有的是那些根本没有在学校工作培训的人。

sentences.en: I went to one school, the school resource officers, they had their metal detector set up.
sentences.zh: 我去过一所学校，学校资源官员设置了金属探测器。

sentences.en: I asked for the principal by name and the school resource officers did not know the principal's name.
sentences.zh: 我指名询问校长，学校资源官员竟然不知道校长的名字。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And this was in Brooklyn, New York.
sentences.zh: 这还是在纽约布鲁克林。

sentences.en: And even some of the language use too, like you described, um, the word obnoxiously.
sentences.zh: 甚至连使用的一些语言也是，就像你描述的，嗯，“令人厌恶地”这个词。

sentences.en: I mean, that is, leaves a lot to interpretation of what that behavior means.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这留下了很大的解读空间，不知道那种行为意味着什么。

sentences.en: It's not very specific.
sentences.zh: 它不是很具体。

sentences.en: So it leaves a lot of room for a student to get removed from the classroom by a resource officer or calling the police.
sentences.zh: 所以它给学生被资源官员带出教室或报警留下了很大的余地。

sentences.en: I want to turn now to students with disabilities who are also disproportionately affected as they represent about 12% of all public school
sentences.zh: 我现在想转向残疾学生，他们也受到了不成比例的影响，因为他们约占所有公立学校学生的12%，

sentences.en: students and account for 25% or more of students referred to law enforcement and clues being arrested for a school related incident or suspended from school.
sentences.zh: 却占了被移交执法部门、因学校相关事件被捕或被停学的学生总数的25%或更多。

sentences.en: So what do you think are some of the underlying cause causes of disparities for students with disabilities?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为残疾学生出现这种差异的根本原因是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think again, there's these broad misunderstandings of development, behavior, mental health, and also just the nature of disability.

sentences.en: dimensions of federal policy.

sentences.en: And so maintaining those kinds of investments become really important and just investing in things that work.

sentences.en: So investing in programs that will support positive mental health outcomes, positive behavioral outcomes, um, research-based social emotional supports.

sentences.en: Um, so a few things before we wrap up, what can parents do with information we've talked about today?
sentences.zh: 嗯，在结束之前，家长们可以利用我们今天讨论的信息做些什么？

sentences.en: I admittedly have difficulty responding to the, you know, what can parents do?
sentences.zh: 我不得不承认，在回答“家长们能做什么？”时，我感到很困难。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: because sometimes I believe that I'm mostly talking to parents with social capital when I respond to questions like, like this.
sentences.zh: 因为有时我相信，当我回答这样的问题时，我主要是与拥有社会资本的家长交谈。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, most parents, they want what's in the best interest of their children, but the way that the system is set up now, a parent who is
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，大多数家长，他们想要的是符合孩子最大利益的事情，但就目前系统的设置方式而言，一个……

sentences.en: college educated, a parent who has certain resources, a parent who knows how to express themselves in a way
sentences.zh: 受过大学教育的家长，一个拥有一定资源的家长，一个知道如何表达自己的人，

sentences.en: that we learn to express ourselves when we go through formal education, uh, they have the edge and that's the reality.
sentences.zh: 就像我们通过正规教育学会表达自己那样，嗯，他们有优势，这就是现实。

sentences.en: Um, so the parents who have that social capital, what I would implore us to do is to look
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以对于那些拥有社会资本的家长，我恳求我们做的是去……

sentences.en: out for parents who don't, um, parents who are working a wage job, parents who take public transportation to
sentences.zh: 关照那些没有社会资本的家长，嗯，那些从事工资劳动工作的家长，那些乘坐公共交通工具……

sentences.en: get their child to school and who may more often be late because of unreliable public transportation,
sentences.zh: 送孩子上学，并且可能因为不可靠的公共交通而更经常迟到的家长，

sentences.en: uh, who have to actually lose money if they were to take off work, to go to a PTA meeting, um, or to go to a parent teacher conference.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果他们为了参加家长会或家长教师会议而请假，实际上会损失钱的家长。

sentences.en: Um, so, so we need to, to look out for, for those, for those parents.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，我们需要去关照那些……那些家长。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, the, the, the, the people who are working in this space, the, the, the advocates and the researchers, uh, like us, um, we need to do a better job
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，你知道，在这个领域工作的人，嗯，倡导者和研究人员，像我们一样，嗯，我们需要做得更好，

sentences.en: of joining forces with other parents and speaking for them.
sentences.zh: 与更多的家长联合起来，为他们代言。

sentences.en: And schools need to do a better job of reaching parents that are not college educated and that, that are working class.
sentences.zh: 学校需要做得更好，去接触那些没有受过大学教育和工人阶级的家长。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: so I know that doesn't necessarily answer the question of what parents should do, but I'm thinking more about the mentality that we should have, uh, as parents when we try to work
sentences.zh: 我知道这未必能回答家长们该怎么做的问题，但我更多是在思考，作为家长，当我们试图共同努力解决这个问题时，我们应该具备什么样的心态。

sentences.en: together to resolve this issue.
sentences.zh: 共同努力解决这个问题。

sentences.en: I think knowing their rights can be really important and that's hard to do because even like, even as I interact with my, my daughter's school, I realize how
sentences.zh: 我认为了解他们的权利非常重要，但这很难做到，因为即使是我在与我女儿的学校互动时，我也意识到，尽管我知道这些，但过程仍然极其繁琐，事情也非常复杂。

sentences.en: knowing what I know, it's still incredibly cumbersome and things are so complicated.
sentences.zh: 尽管我知道这些，但过程仍然极其繁琐，事情也非常复杂。

sentences.en: But I think to the extent that, um, students can, or parents can find and access those resources that have been
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在一定程度上，学生或家长可以找到并利用那些通过各种技术援助机制为他们开发的资源。

sentences.en: developed for them through a variety of different technical assistance mechanisms that are out there.
sentences.zh: 通过各种现有的技术援助机制为他们开发的资源。

sentences.en: So for parents with disabilities in particular, there's a whole host of federally funded centers that have developed, um, guidance materials specifically for families, but also,
sentences.zh: 因此，特别是对于残疾学生的家长，有许多联邦资助的中心，它们不仅为家庭开发了专门的指导材料，而且，

sentences.en: um, for teachers in school districts, there are equity assistance centers and I'm affiliated for
sentences.zh: 对于学区的教师，也有公平援助中心，我所在的地区就有这样一个中心，它们主要是作为学校的一种主动资源，

sentences.en: the one in my region that they're primarily there as a proactive resource for schools that are going
sentences.zh: 它们主要是作为学校的一种主动资源，旨在帮助学校避免受到民权办公室的调查。

sentences.en: to get themselves, um, as a way to avoid investigations with the office of civil rights.
sentences.zh: 旨在帮助学校避免受到民权办公室的调查。

sentences.en: But a lot of them also develop information for families about what their rights are.
sentences.zh: 但其中许多中心也为家庭提供了关于他们权利的信息。

sentences.en: Um, Westlaw is a nice resource, um, for, for families, but I think just, um, frankly, you can Google a lot of this stuff.
sentences.zh: Westlaw 是一个不错的资源，但坦率地说，你可以通过谷歌搜索到很多这类信息。

sentences.en: Like, what should I do if my, my student is expelled?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我的学生被开除了，我该怎么办？

sentences.en: What are my rights if my student is suspended?
sentences.zh: 如果我的学生被停课了，我有什么权利？

sentences.en: Um, because a lot of it's about knowing the right questions to ask.
sentences.zh: 因为很多时候，关键在于知道该问什么样的问题。

sentences.en: And even then they can still encounter a lot of difficulty, but the first step is just knowing how to advocate effectively.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，他们仍可能遇到很多困难，但第一步只是学会如何有效地进行倡导。

sentences.en: And luckily there's a variety of information online to help with that.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，网上有各种各样的信息可以提供帮助。

sentences.en: And what about individual school districts and teachers?
sentences.zh: 那么各个学区和老师呢？

sentences.en: Is there other things they can take away from what we've talked about today and see if they can improve these disparities in them and their schools?
sentences.zh: 他们还能从我们今天讨论的内容中汲取什么，看看能否改善他们学校中存在的这些差异吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Teachers need to communicate with their students and their families a lot more.
sentences.zh: 老师们需要与学生及其家庭进行更多的沟通。

sentences.en: Uh, a lot of times, uh, the problematic behavior that they are confronted with, uh, they'd understand it better if they just talk to them and they would contextualize it better.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，他们所面临的问题行为，如果他们能与学生沟通，就能更好地理解并将其置于具体情境中去分析。

sentences.en: I remember asking the group of teachers, I said, how do you feel about students who doze off in your class?
sentences.zh: 我记得我问过一群老师，我说，你们对在课堂上打瞌睡的学生有什么感觉？

sentences.en: And all of them, you know, they didn't like it.
sentences.zh: 他们所有人都说，他们不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: They, they thought it was disrespectful and they used that terminology.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这很不尊重人，并使用了这样的措辞。

sentences.en: I said, well, what if you talk to the student and you found out that, uh, they were dozing off because they, their parent had a significant
sentences.zh: 我说，如果你们和学生谈过，发现他们打瞌睡是因为家里有重要的人，

sentences.en: other in the house, had a boyfriend or girlfriend in the house, uh, that they were afraid of, and they saw them looking at them a certain way.
sentences.zh: 比如家里有让他们感到害怕的男朋友或女朋友，而且他们看到那个人用某种眼神盯着他们看。

sentences.en: And they were afraid that that person was going to sneak into their bed.
sentences.zh: 他们担心那个人会溜进他们的房间。

sentences.en: How'd you feel about them dozing off?
sentences.zh: 那你对他们打瞌睡有什么感觉？

sentences.en: And then they all immediately became very sympathetic.
sentences.zh: 然后他们立刻都变得非常同情。

sentences.en: Um, but the reality is that a lot of times when you see things like dozing off or even,
sentences.zh: 但现实情况是，很多时候当你看到打瞌睡，甚至，

sentences.en: you know, disrespect oppositional behavior, a lot of times it comes from a place that we might
sentences.zh: 你知道，不尊重或对抗行为，很多时候其根源是我们如果了解了细节就能理解的，但你必须足够关心才能去了解这些细节。

sentences.en: understand if we just got the details, but you have to care enough to get those details.
sentences.zh: 我们如果了解了细节就能理解的，但你必须足够关心才能去了解这些细节。

sentences.en: Uh, so I would say open up the communication, uh, and, you know, just, just understand, um, teachers can also, um, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我建议敞开沟通，并且，你知道，去理解，老师们也可以，

sentences.en: take their professional development very seriously, uh, and understand that, you know, I know that they have options on, on what they could, you know, do in their PD.
sentences.zh: 非常认真地对待他们的专业发展，并且明白，我知道他们在专业发展方面有选择权。

sentences.en: Um, you know, they can, you know, learn about this new way to teach math, or they could learn about how to develop empathy, our cultural competence and things like that.
sentences.zh: 他们可以学习这种教数学的新方法，或者学习如何培养同理心、文化素养之类的东西。

sentences.en: Um, but you know, they've, in their schooling, they've learned about, you know, all the things that they need to learn about, but professional development is the one
sentences.zh: 但在他们的学校教育中，他们已经学习了所有需要学习的东西，但专业发展是他们真正深入探讨这些问题的唯一机会。

sentences.en: opportunity they really have to really get into these issues.
sentences.zh: 专业发展是他们真正深入探讨这些问题的唯一机会。

sentences.en: Uh, and you know, I'll talk about my own frustration as someone who does professional development is going into a district where I know
sentences.zh: 作为一名从事专业发展工作的人，我感到沮丧的是，当我进入一个学区时，我知道

sentences.en: that the teaching force is only about 20% people of color, but yet in the 200 people who signed up for my workshop, it's about 70% people of color.
sentences.zh: 那里的教师队伍中只有约 20% 是有色人种，但在报名参加我研讨会的 200 人中，约 70% 是有色人种。

sentences.en: And that happens a lot.
sentences.zh: 这种情况经常发生。

sentences.en: So a lot of times the people that really need this information the most are not the people that's getting it.
sentences.zh: 所以很多时候，最需要这些信息的人反而没有得到这些信息。

sentences.en: And, and even the, the, the white teachers who will be in the professional development, just the questions
sentences.zh: 即使是参加专业发展的白人教师，从他们提出的问题中，

sentences.en: that they ask a lot of times I can tell that they have learned, you know, they at least have a base knowledge of this.
sentences.zh: 我能看出他们已经学过，或者至少对这些有基础知识。

sentences.en: Um, but there are too many educators out there who don't really see this as their issue.
sentences.zh: 但仍有太多的教育工作者并不真正认为这是他们的问题。

sentences.en: And so they need to take that, you know, more seriously.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要更认真地对待这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think to the extent people can invest that time and energy into unlearning biases and, and learning cultural responsive, non-discriminatory practices.
sentences.zh: 我认为，只要人们能够投入时间和精力去消除偏见，学习文化响应式、非歧视性的实践，

sentences.en: Um, also investing time in developing behavior management skills.
sentences.zh: 同时投入时间培养行为管理技能。

sentences.en: So this might be through, um, individual or classroom level positive behavior interventions or supports or ideally a school wide, a PBIS system.
sentences.zh: 这可以通过个人或课堂层面的积极行为干预或支持，或者理想情况下，全校范围的 PBIS 系统来实现。

sentences.en: Um, there are also a variety of strategies and programs available to support positive student teacher relationships.
sentences.zh: 还有各种各样的策略和项目可以支持建立积极的师生关系。

sentences.en: Um, which again, the research shows that can reduce some of these behavioral challenges.
sentences.zh: 研究再次表明，这可以减少其中一些行为挑战。

sentences.en: Um, also either at the classroom level or the school wide level, investing in ways to improve school climate.
sentences.zh: 此外，无论是在课堂层面还是全校层面，都要投入资源改善学校氛围。

sentences.en: So again, there's programs, strategies that are there.
sentences.zh: 同样，有很多现成的项目和策略。

sentences.en: Um, they don't have to constantly be reinventing the wheel, but rather taking advantage of the knowledge and resources that are already out there.
sentences.zh: 他们不必总是重复发明轮子，而是应该利用现有的知识和资源。

sentences.en: Is there anything a general listener can do?
sentences.zh: 普通听众能做些什么吗？

sentences.en: You can take action on?
sentences.zh: 你能采取什么行动？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, different people are different places in, in this issue.
sentences.zh: 不同的人在这个问题上处于不同的位置。

sentences.en: You know, some, some of the listeners, they, they may have, uh, uh, their own children in schools that have these issues.
sentences.zh: 有些听众可能自己的孩子就在有这些问题的学校里。

sentences.en: So there are certain things that they could do.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以做一些特定的事情。

sentences.en: Uh, but, you know, just the general public, we can use more people speaking out against certain things.
sentences.zh: 但对于普通大众来说，我们需要更多人站出来反对某些事情。

sentences.en: And, um, you know, there's a lot of times I'll see articles about, you know, suspensions are, um, you know, things that
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我会看到关于停课的文章，或者，

sentences.en: happen, you know, like in, like what happened in, in, um, at Montgomery County schools recently,
sentences.zh: 比如最近在蒙哥马利县学校发生的事情，

sentences.en: where, uh, someone, a student had to talk to police officers because he bought toy money to school and somebody, um, uh, said that it might be counterfeit.
sentences.zh: 一名学生不得不与警察交谈，因为他带了玩具钱到学校，有人说那可能是伪钞。

sentences.en: Um, but a lot of times on these message boards, you'll see, uh, people who have just really baked into this idea of, well, you know, students are out of control.
sentences.zh: 但在这些留言板上，你经常会看到一些人，他们真的固执地认为，学生们已经失控了。

sentences.en: We need to get them in line and all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们需要让他们守规矩，诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: And a lot of, you know, there's this, that saying, you know, the, um, empty wagons are usually the loudest or empty wagons are the loudeSt. Our shallow creeks are the most noisy.
sentences.zh: 俗话说，空车最响，或者浅溪最吵。

sentences.en: Uh, and a lot of times with the general public, I see people who talk the most, uh, have the most ignorant things to say about the topic.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，在公众中，我看到那些说得最多的人，对这个话题的看法往往是最无知的。

sentences.en: So, uh, I know that people who listen to this podcast are very smart.
sentences.zh: 我知道听这个播客的人都很聪明。

sentences.en: Uh, they are not the empty wagons are a shallow Creek, but, but people who really can get into this issue.
sentences.zh: 他们不是那些空车或浅溪，而是真正能深入探讨这个问题的人。

sentences.en: So, um, we need them on message boards and we need them talking out, uh, when they have an opportunity, uh, we need
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要他们在留言板上发声，我们需要他们在有机会时站出来说话，我们需要

sentences.en: them to be the counterbalance to, um, to this issue, uh, so that, you know, more people are aware.
sentences.zh: 他们成为这个问题的制衡力量，让更多人意识到这一点。

sentences.en: I think this is one of those examples where that notion of like giving psychology away,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个很好的例子，说明了那种“普及心理学”的理念，

sentences.en: I think psychology has a lot to bring to bear about how we can do this better so that we see better outcomes with students.
sentences.zh: 我认为心理学在如何做得更好方面有很多贡献，这样我们就能看到学生们有更好的表现。

sentences.en: And so to the extent that everybody's, uh, feels empowered to speak up.
sentences.zh: 因此，只要每个人都感到有能力站出来说话。

sentences.en: So it's not just the, those empty wagons, um, dominating the conversations, but just reminding people that, again, we know, we know how to respond to this well.
sentences.zh: 这样就不会只有那些“空车”主导对话，而是提醒人们，我们知道如何很好地应对这个问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So let's do that.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们这样做吧。

sentences.en: And it's, we're probably going to have to advocate for it a lot and repeatedly.
sentences.zh: 我们可能需要反复地、多次地为此进行倡导。

sentences.en: Um, but I think there's a lot of potential for change because again, I mean, nobody, I suspect nobody goes into teaching or working in schools because they hate children.
sentences.zh: 但我认为变革的潜力很大，因为没有人是因为讨厌孩子才去教书或在学校工作的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Every, I hope people who are
sentences.zh: 我希望人们从事教育是因为

sentences.en: belief in, um, fostering the development of future generations as part of it.
sentences.zh: 相信培养未来一代是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And so if we can link it back to that kind of fundamental ideal, hopefully we can affect change, but also just
sentences.zh: 如果我们能将其与这种基本理想联系起来，希望我们能推动变革，同时也

sentences.en: kind of give away psychology because we know so much that can help to improve this.
sentences.zh: 普及心理学，因为我们掌握了很多有助于改善现状的知识。

sentences.en: So let's help that to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们共同促成这一点。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for joining us, Dr. Sullivan, Dr. Tolson, obviously a lot, a lot of work to do in this area, but you left us on a, on a hopeful note.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您加入我们，Sullivan 博士，Tolson 博士，显然在这个领域还有很多工作要做，但你们给我们留下了一个充满希望的结尾。

sentences.en: So that can be done and psychology and psychologists can do a lot to address this issue.
sentences.zh: 所以这是可以做到的，心理学和心理学家可以在解决这个问题上发挥很大作用。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢您的时间。
